events.title: C programming language takes shape at Bell Labs
events.summary: Dennis Ritchie evolved C from B during 1971–73; 1972 was the most creative period for the language and first compiler.
events.about: C is a systems language — close to the machine, but portable. Used to write operating systems (Unix/Linux kernels), databases, embedded [firmware], game engines, and anything that needs speed and direct memory control. C still underpins most [OS] and runtime code today.

narrative.whyChosen: C became the systems language of Unix and later the foundation for C++, [Objective-C], Go, and much of modern infrastructure.
narrative.whyImportant: It added a practical type system to B and enabled rewriting Unix in a portable [high-level language].
narrative.problemSolved: B was too limited for the PDP-11 byte architecture and growing Unix [kernel] needs.

events.title: Prolog language created
events.summary: In fall 1972, Alain Colmerauer and Philippe Roussel built the first Prolog — a language where you state facts and rules, and the computer searches for answers.
events.about: In Prolog you write what is true ('Bob is a parent of Ann') and what rules follow ('a grandparent is a parent of a parent'), then ask questions ('Who are Ann's grandparents?'). The engine finds answers by searching possibilities. It powered [expert system]s, language tools, and AI research, and influenced how later languages handle automated reasoning.

narrative.whyChosen: Prolog was the first widely used language where you describe problems as logic instead of step-by-step instructions.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed that rule-based, declarative programs could run real applications — from language research to industrial [expert system]s.
narrative.problemSolved: Colmerauer's team needed one tool for both parsing human language and automated reasoning, without building separate custom engines for each.

events.title: Karen Spärck Jones publishes IDF
events.summary: Karen Spärck Jones introduced inverse document frequency (IDF) in 1972 — a cornerstone of search ranking and information retrieval.
events.about: IDF weights rare terms higher in search — the 'idf' in tf-idf used by Elasticsearch, Lucene, and early Google. Her work predates the web but powers every search engine developers integrate with.

narrative.whyChosen: IDF is foundational math behind modern search ranking.
narrative.whyImportant: It quantified term importance across document collections.
narrative.problemSolved: Keyword matching alone ranked common words as important as distinctive ones.

events.title: Jon Postel begins Internet numbering stewardship
events.summary: Jon Postel took on socket-number and protocol assignment duties in 1972 — the functions later formalized as IANA, though that name was not used until the 1980s.
events.about: Postel's stewardship kept the internet's naming and numbering coherent as it grew from [ARPANET] research to a global network. He was the RFC Editor and IANA administrator until his death in 1998.

narrative.whyChosen: Postel's quiet governance made decentralized internet growth possible.
narrative.whyImportant: IANA assignments let independent networks interoperate without a central authority.
narrative.problemSolved: Growing packet networks needed consistent protocol numbers and document editing.
